prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1069; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed the first notice of loss for the left-turn collision. Insured vehicle was turning left at an intersection when it was struck by an oncoming vehicle that was proceeding straight. Police report requested. Initial photos of both vehicles obtained from the insured.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Claimant reports neck and back pain beginning shortly after the collision and is seeking medical evaluation. Claimant is not represented by an attorney and has asked how the claim process works. Explained the coverage review steps and the need for medical documentation.

Entry 3: Contacted the insured to confirm the account of the collision. Insured states the left-turn signal had turned green and the oncoming vehicle entered the intersection on a late yellow or red. Insured's statement recorded. Witness information requested from the insured, none currently available.

Entry 4: Received preliminary medical records from the claimant's treating provider. Diagnosis listed as cervical and lumbar strain with muscle spasm. Treatment plan includes physical therapy and follow-up in several weeks. Records placed in the file pending full review and reconciliation with the vehicle damage estimate.

Entry 5: Vehicle inspection completed. Damage pattern to the front quarter panel of the insured vehicle and rear driver-side area of the claimant vehicle is consistent with the reported angle of impact. Liability assessment in progress. Claimant advised that a settlement offer will not be made until the medical treatment is complete and records are received.
